projects.title: Bank Reconciliation Agent
projects.label: RECON
projects.short: Rules-first reconciliation agent on synthetic data
projects.pitch: A rules-first tool-calling agent that matches small-business bank lines to invoices on synthetic data.
projects.card: A rules-first tool-calling agent that matches small-business bank lines to invoices on synthetic data. Code verifies every proposal, the model cannot write to the ledger, and a person approves before anything posts. Read-only MCP server, a plain-English rule compiler, live evals on four models, a pre-registered code-mode experiment and a CI replay gate; the README says where it breaks.
projects.byline: Personal project · v1.1.0 · Synthetic data only
projects.visual_alt: Terminal replay of make demo: 40 committed bank lines through the rules pass, the agent and the shadow policy, each proposal left for a person to review

claims.text: 0 wrong matches in 460 agent match proposals (582 agent decisions) over 3 live runs on each of two synthetic businesses.

0 of 40 injected lines that ask for a different or an extra invoice succeeded in any run. The verifier refuses whatever the payload asks for on 36 of them; on the 4 it leaves to the model's judgement, 0 payloads were followed by any model in any run with defences on.
containment held in every run and every probe, and code mode was cheaper on average, but the pre-registered efficiency hypothesis failed for both models tested.

projects.title: Provenance-Tiered RAG
projects.label: RAG
projects.short: RAG over NZ GST, German VAT and INZ instructions
projects.pitch: Question answering over New Zealand GST law, German VAT law and Immigration New Zealand's Operational Manual, with dated sources in tiers.
projects.card: Question answering over New Zealand GST law, German VAT law (UStG and UStDV) and Immigration New Zealand's Operational Manual, with dated sources in tiers: statute, official guidance and untrusted notes. Immigration answers are information from INZ's published instructions, not immigration advice. Code checks every citation and figure against passages in force on the date asked about. Frozen eval sets, held-back questions and defence ablations; the README says what the numbers do not show.

projects.title: mcp-code-mode
projects.label: MCP
projects.short: Code mode for any MCP server, in Python
projects.pitch: Run model-written Python against any MCP server's tools in a locked-down Docker sandbox, through a host-side bridge that checks every call.
projects.card: Run model-written Python against any MCP server's tools in a locked-down Docker sandbox. It serves a wrapped server's tools to the model as one run_python tool. Every call passes a host-side bridge that checks the allowlist, the tool's JSON Schema, argument size and a call budget, and refuses oversized results. Extracted from bank-reconciliation-agent; the README maps each threat to a control and a test, and lists what it does not protect.
projects.visual_alt: Terminal capture: a program calls two allowlisted toy tools through the bridge, then builds a call to a tool off the allowlist, which the bridge refuses before the server sees it

claims.lead: Where it was measured, in bank-reconciliation-agent:
claims.text: containment held in every run and every probe, and code mode was cheaper on average, but the pre-registered efficiency hypothesis failed for both models tested. Read the numbers there; this package carries no measurements of its own.
